text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been present, and did they start suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) with Horner's Syndrome and Brachial Plexus Palsy.

The combination of progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, unexplained weight loss, and your history of smoking and diabetes is highly suggestive of an apical lung tumor compressing the brachial plexus. Given your bodybuilding and steroid use, we must also rule out metabolic myopathies or other compressive neuropathies. I am requesting immediate imaging to visualize the apical lung and brachial plexus.
